study_identification_part.si4_title: Lifespan development of thalamic nuclei and characterizing thalamic nuclei abnormalities in schizophrenia using normative modeling

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and aims clearly state objectives: to characterize age effects on thalamic nuclei with normative models, apply them to an independent schizophrenia cohort to quantify deviation frequencies, and relate deviations to cognition, highlighting precision medicine relevance. These statements satisfy both criteria: explicit research questions and the purpose of applying normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "we characterized the development of thalamic nuclei volumes using normative models generated from the Human Connectome Project Lifespan datasets ... then applied them to an independent clinical cohort to determine the frequency of thalamic volume deviations in people with schizophrenia ... the degree of deviation ... correlated with the severity of cognitive impairment ... Normative modeling enables the identification of these individuals, which is a necessary step toward precision medicine."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: This study builds a new normative model using HCP Lifespan datasets. It (1) describes eligibility/exclusions for the reference cohort: twins randomly removed; scans with poor quality or segmentation failure excluded; (2) specifies image quality standards: visual inspection for artifacts and segmentation QC; (3) reports the final sample size (n=1952) and points to CONSORT-style exclusion details in Supplementary Materials. These meet all listed criteria for NEW models.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text:
"After randomly removing twins to avoid biasing the normative lifespan model and excluding individuals with poor quality scans or segmentation failures, the final sample was 1952 ... Detailed demographics and exclusion information ... in the Supplementary Materials." 
"All T1 images underwent visual inspection for visible artifacts, including motion artifacts, before thalamic segmentation." 
"Individuals were excluded ... if their thalamus segmentation included voxels outside the thalamus or missed voxels within the thalamus."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Covariates age, sex, race, and eTIV are modeled in GAMLSS; a family-level random intercept is included. Multi-site effects are addressed via ComBat harmonization with site/scanner as batches and age, sex, race, diagnosis as preserved covariates. This satisfies consideration of demographic covariates and multi-site handling.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text:
"We used GAMLSS ... after controlling for race, estimated total intracranial volume including a random effect for family ... natural cubic spline function with 2 equally-spaced knots over the age range (5 to 100 years)." 
"To account for site effects, we used ComBat to adjust for site and scanner effects ... with age, sex, race, and diagnoses included as covariates to adjust for during harmonization."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort sources are explicitly named: HCP S1200 (ConnectomeDB), HCP Development (NIH Data Archive), and HCP Aging (NIH Data Archive), with sample sizes and age ranges.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Normative modeling ... using data from the Human Connectome Project (HCP) Lifespan Studies ... the original HCP S1200 sample ... obtained from ConnectomeDB ... HCP Development and Aging ... obtained from the NIH Data Archive."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Per guide, acquisition protocol details are not required when using secondary data. The reference cohort data are from existing HCP datasets rather than primary collection in this study.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: "The HCP Lifespan Cohort was collected at four locations across multiple scanners ... Imaging acquisition parameters for each project are presented in the Supplementary Materials."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is described: HCP PreFreeSurfer pipeline applied to raw T1 images to produce bias-field corrected T1s; schizophrenia cohort did not require preprocessing. Quality control included visual inspection for artifacts prior to segmentation.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "Preprocessing of the raw T1 images from the HCP Lifespan Cohort was done using the PreFreeSurfer HCP pipeline ... outputs bias field corrected structural T1 images in 'native' subject space. ... All T1 images underwent visual inspection for visible artifacts, including motion artifacts, before thalamic segmentation."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No train/validation/test splits, cross-validation, or other internal partitioning of the HCP reference cohort are described. The model is instead assessed using an independent healthy control group (external validation), but no internal data partition strategy is reported.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text:
"After randomly removing twins ... the final sample was 1952 ..." (no mention of internal split) ; 
"The validity of this model was tested using our healthy control group ... a median of 85.3% of healthy individuals fell within the 90% range" (external validation).

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The normative model trained on HCP was applied to an independent dataset of healthy individuals (the healthy control subset of the schizophrenia cohort) to evaluate coverage of centile ranges, demonstrating external validation.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "The validity of this model was tested using our healthy control group, and we identified the proportion of individuals who fell within 90% of the population. Across all thalamic subdivisions, a median of 85.3% of healthy individuals fell within the 90% range, indicating that the normative models generalized reasonably well to an independent sample."

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is specified as GAMLSS with natural cubic splines (2 knots) over age using a generalized gamma distribution; link functions are defined (log for mu and sigma, identity for nu). Covariates include age, sex, race, eTIV with family random intercept. Software for harmonization (neuroCombat R package) is cited; code repositories are provided for pipelines and analyses.

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: A quantitative calibration metric (coverage of the 90% centile range) is reported when applying the model to an independent healthy cohort (85.3% within the 90% range). However, no explicit fit/error metrics or calibration assessments are reported for the reference cohort partitions, and no internal validation metrics are presented.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Across all thalamic subdivisions, a median of 85.3% of healthy individuals fell within the 90% range, indicating that the normative models generalized reasonably well to an independent sample."

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No data partitioning (e.g., train/validation/test or cross-validation folds) is reported for the reference cohort; therefore characteristics by partition are not applicable.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: "After randomly removing twins ... the final sample was 1952 ..." (no partitions described).

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Reproducibility is supported by public code and pipeline availability (GitHub links for THOMAS docker and statistical analyses) and clear data source descriptions. Software/library versions are not fully specified for all components (e.g., GAMLSS version not given), and trained model artifacts are not provided, so criteria are partially met.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text:
"Data for normative modeling were derived from publicly available datasets. ... Neuroimaging data storage and processing took place at ... XNAT." 
"Neuroimaging processing pipelines were containerized using Singularity ... accessible through GitHub (https://github.com/baxpr/thomasdocker). Code for statistical analyses is accessible through GitHub (https://github.com/Woodward-Lab/NormModThalamicNuclei)."

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical cohort eligibility is described (SCID DSM-IV diagnoses; detailed exclusion criteria). Image quality procedures are specified (visual inspection; segmentation QC). Final sample sizes and references to exclusion reasons via CONSORT diagram are provided.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text:
"Diagnoses were confirmed ... using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV ... Exclusion criteria included ... significant medical or neurological illness ... premorbid IQ less than 65, substance abuse or dependence ... MRI contraindications ... Healthy individuals were excluded if ... psychiatric illnesses or a first-degree relative with a psychotic illness ... final sample included 211 healthy controls ... and 234 individuals with a schizophrenia spectrum diagnosis ... See Supplementary Materials for the CONSORT diagram detailing people we excluded for diagnosis or image quality." 
"All T1 images underwent visual inspection ... before thalamic segmentation. ... Individuals were excluded ... if their thalamus segmentation included voxels outside the thalamus or missed voxels within the thalamus."

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses relate deviation scores to a clinical cognitive measure (SCIP composite z-score), which is beyond basic demographics. However, other clinical covariates such as medication status or illness duration are not modeled as covariates in the deviation analyses.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "We tested associations between deviation (centile) scores and cognitive function ... Cognitive function was measured with the SCIP composite z-score."

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: The clinical cohort is described as a repository study drawing from three neuroimaging projects, with acquisition at a single location (three parameter sets) and references to supplementary acquisition details.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text:
"Individual deviations in thalamus volumes were drawn from a repository study comprising 643 individuals who participated in one of three neuroimaging projects (CT00762866, R01MH070560, R01MH102266)." 
"The Schizophrenia Cohort was collected at a single location with three sets of parameters (see Supplemental Materials)."

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes are provided (211 HC; 234 SZ). Demographic variables and clinical characteristics (e.g., PANSS, WTAR) are reported in Table 1 and extended in Supplementary Tables.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text:
"Our final sample included 211 healthy controls ... and 234 individuals with a schizophrenia spectrum diagnosis ... Basic participant demographics for this sample are included in Table 1. Expanded demographics can be found in the Supplementary Materials." 
"Supplementary Table 2. Extended demographics for the schizophrenia cohort."

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Clinical assessment tools and procedures are specified: SCID for DSM-IV diagnoses, PANSS for symptoms, WTAR for premorbid IQ, and SCIP for cognitive assessment, including measure descriptions.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text:
"Diagnoses were confirmed ... using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV ... Clinical symptoms ... assessed with the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS), and premorbid IQ ... Wechsler Test for Adult Reading (WTAR)." 
"Neuropsychological functioning in the Schizophrenia Cohort was assessed with the Screen for Cognitive Impairment in Psychiatry (SCIP) ... five sub-tests ..."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The study defines deviation thresholds (infra-normal: below 5th centile; supra-normal: above 95th centile) and uses these to interpret individual-level abnormalities. Clinical implications are discussed via associations between deviation scores and cognitive impairment, including that deviation-based associations were stronger than with raw volumes.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text:
"We then calculated the proportion of individuals in the schizophrenia group with infra-normal (below 5th centile), and supra-normal (above 95th centile) volumes ..." 
"we observed significant associations in the schizophrenia group using centile values but not the standardized raw volumes ..."
